definitions.explanation: Short form of {総理大臣|そうりだいじん}, the prime minister of Japan. This abbreviated form is very commonly used in everyday speech and media.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧{総理|そうり}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{決|き}まった→決まる：01233_kimaru⟧。
examples.english: A new prime minister has been decided.

examples.japanese: {総理|そうり}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{記者会見|きしゃかいけん}→記者会見：19954_kishakaiken⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|ひら}いた→開く：01979_hiraku⟧。
examples.english: The prime minister held a press conference.

examples.japanese: {総理|そうり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{支持率|しじりつ}→支持率：17086_shijiritsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大幅|おおはば}→大幅：12170_oohaba⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{下|さ}がっている→下がる：01188_sagaru⟧。
examples.english: The prime minister's approval rating has dropped significantly.

notes:
USAGE:
Abbreviation of ⟦{総理大臣|そうりだいじん}→総理大臣：15205_souridaijin⟧ (prime minister). In news and conversation, {総理|そうり} is far more common than the full form. When addressing or referring to a specific prime minister, the pattern is surname + {総理|そうり} (e.g., ⟦{田中|たなか}→田中：09528_tanaka⟧{総理|そうり}). The formal title used in official documents is {内閣総理大臣|ないかくそうりだいじん}.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{首相|しゅしょう}→首相：03217_shushou⟧: prime minister (used more in news reporting, applies to any country's PM)
- ⟦{大統領|だいとうりょう}→大統領：03418_daitouryou⟧: president (of a country)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{総理大臣|そうりだいじん}→総理大臣：15205_souridaijin⟧: prime minister (full form)
- {総理|そうり}⟦{官邸|かんてい}→官邸：12305_kantei⟧: prime minister's official residence
- {総理|そうり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{支持率|しじりつ}→支持率：17086_shijiritsu⟧: prime minister's approval rating
- {総理|そうり}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{就任|しゅうにん}→就任：12368_shuunin⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: take office as prime minister
